description: This pie chart, from the paper "Evaluation of Speaker Anonymization on Emotional Speech," visually represents the distribution of six distinct emotional states, each occupying a separate slice of the circle. The chart is divided into six segments, with each labeled and accompanied by a percentage value: "Frustration" (25.1%, light blue), "Neutral" (23.1%, dark blue), "Happiness" (8.1%, light blue), "Excitement" (14.1%, red), "Anger" (14.9%, yellow), and "Surprise" (14.7%, orange). The percentages are displayed directly within each corresponding slice, and the chart includes a legend that maps the colors to the emotional categories. The slices are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top, with "Frustration" being the largest segment, followed by "Neutral," then "Anger" and "Excitement" of nearly equal size, "Surprise" slightly smaller than "Anger," and "Happiness" as the smallest segment. The chart does not show any exploded or emphasized slices, and the segments appear to be ordered by descending size, though not perfectly aligned.
